project: Automatos AI Platform — PRD-224 The Ticket Lane: Auto as Line Manager (Auto-as-Manager wave, chain 2/6)
description: STACKED branch: ralph/prd-224-ticket-lane ← ralph/prd-227-board-light-up (chain 2/6; PRD-227's agent-move SSE + blocked/failed parity are IN your tree — build on them, never duplicate; diff scope for review = merge-base vs the 227 branch). userStories.title: [CRITICAL] Ambiguous agent-name resolution silently dispatches to the WRONG agent instead of asking in-thread
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (chain 2/6 adversarial review + code-reviewer, both independent). consumers/chatbot/auto.py:909-926 _match_roster_agent does exact-match first, then a bidirectional substring fallback ('if an in target or target in an: return a.id, a.name') that returns on the FIRST hit with NO ambiguity check. The roster source _active_agents (auto.py:886-901) has NO order_by, so when >1 agent substring-matches, which one wins is whatever order Postgres returns (nondeterministic). Concrete failure: workspace has active agents 'Jim Whitfield' and 'Jimmy Cross'; user says 'Have Jim send the invoice reminder now'; classifier extracts target_agent='Jim'; no exact match, so the contains loop fires and BOTH match ('jim' is a prefix of 'jimmy') — the first row returned silently becomes target_agent_name, resolved=True, and build_assign_directive (auto.py:89-128) tells Auto to file+start the ticket for the wrong agent, immediately (in_progress) and auto-supervised, with zero user visibility. create_board_task (handlers_board_tasks.py:85-90) then faithfully assigns the real ticket to that wrong agent by exact name. This directly violates the baked decision + PRD Wave-1 AC 'Ambiguous/unknown agent name -> Auto asks in-thread rather than guessing' (docs/PRDS/PRD-224-AUTO-TICKET-LANE.md:78) and the function's own docstring claim 'NEVER a fuzzy best-guess'. Short agent names ('Ops','AI') compound it — they substring-match almost any longer target. NOT cross-workspace (roster filters workspace_id; cache key is workspace-prefixed) and a stale cached id is re-verified at tool time — the defect is specifically the missing ambiguity check on the within-workspace contains-match. Existing coverage test_match_roster_contains_possessive (tests/test_prd224_assign_lane.py:151-154) only exercises a SINGLE-agent roster, so the multi-match case is untested. Fix direction: when the exact-match loop misses AND the contains check yields other-than-exactly-one candidate (0 or >=2), return (None, None) so the turn takes the ask-in-thread path — never a first-of-many pick.
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — _match_roster_agent (auto.py): exact-name loop UNCHANGED (a single exact hit still resolves first). When exact misses, the contains fallback now collects EVERY match into a dict keyed by agent id and resolves ONLY when len(matches)==1 (exactly one distinct agent); 0 or ≥2 distinct matches return (None, None). Order-independent (dict-by-id, never first-row), so target_agent_id stays None and apply_assign_bias/build_assign_directive take the resolved=False ask-in-thread branch.

DONE — tests/test_prd224_assign_lane.py +5: test_match_roster_ambiguous_contains_asks_not_guesses ('Jim' vs 'Jim Whitfield'+'Jimmy Cross' → (None,None)); _ambiguous_is_order_independent (both roster orders → None); _two_short_names_are_ambiguous ('AI Ops' vs 'Ops'/'AI'); _single_contains_still_resolves_amid_others ('my accountant agent' → (7,'Accountant') amid a Researcher); _ambiguous_match_drives_ask_in_thread_directive (platform_list_agents + 'Do NOT guess or auto-pick'). userStories.title: [CRITICAL] ASSIGN immediate-start races the board dispatcher — the same ticket can EXECUTE twice
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (chain 2/6 adversarial review + code-reviewer, both independent). The ASSIGN imperative-default path (the baked 'START IMMEDIATELY' case) has Auto do two back-to-back tool calls per build_assign_directive (auto.py:99-119): (1) platform_create_task (lands status='assigned' since the agent resolved and no explicit status is passed — handlers_board_tasks.py:98) then (2) platform_update_task_status -> 'in_progress'. US-001's NEW _notify_dispatch_safe on create (handlers_board_tasks.py:164-165, fired by _is_dispatch_claimable when assigned+agent) wakes board_dispatcher.run_dispatch_loop (started in main.py:585) at sub-second LISTEN/NOTIFY latency; the dispatcher's claim_tasks (services/board_dispatcher.py:64-181, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) flips the row to in_progress and calls _launch_task_execution (board_dispatcher.py:474) = launch #1. Auto's step-2 update_board_task_status then launches AGAIN: the inline trigger at handlers_board_tasks.py:421 ('if new_status == in_progress and task.assigned_agent_id: _launch_task_execution(...)') has NO old_status/lease guard, so it re-launches even though the dispatcher already claimed the row = launch #2. Both call AgentFactory.execute_with_prompt concurrently for the same task_id — the agent's REAL side effects (emails, external API calls, writes) run twice; the only mutual-exclusion is the terminal status-write at the end (second finisher sees status != in_progress and skips its DB write), which MASKS the double-run on the board. The codebase already knows this guard is required: run_task_now (api/board_tasks.py:871) does 'if task.status == in_progress: raise 409' before calling the shared _redispatch_task, whose docstring even states 'Caller guarantees the task is not already in_progress' — that guard is simply absent on the chat-side update path. SAME-CLASS second site: watch_actions.run_board_task_action (services/watch_actions.py) calls _redispatch_task with no in-progress re-check (narrower window — the ticker only reaches it after a terminal read — but a human 'Run Now' or other restart between the terminal read and the decider's rerun re-opens it). This is the default 'start now' path, not an edge case. Fix direction: make the transition-to-in_progress launch conditional on the prior status (skip the launch when the row is already in_progress, mirroring run_task_now's 409/claim_tasks idiom), and add the same in-progress guard to run_board_task_action before _redispatch_task.
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — update_board_task_status (handlers_board_tasks.py): the inline _launch_task_execution now fires only when new_status=='in_progress' AND assigned agent AND old_status!='in_progress' (old_status is captured at the read). By the time Auto's back-to-back status write runs, board_dispatcher.claim_tasks has usually already claimed the row (flipping it to in_progress) — the guard mirrors the Run-Now route's own check at api/board_tasks.py:871, so a write of in_progress onto an already-in_progress row launches ZERO extra executions. triggered_execution now returns the real 'launched' flag (honest, no longer claims a launch it skipped).

userStories.title: [MEDIUM] ASSIGN directive scripts the 'supervised' confirmation unconditionally — dishonest when AUTO_TICKET_WATCH is off / no watch attached
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (chain 2/6 adversarial review; related strand flagged by code-reviewer). build_assign_directive (auto.py:99-119) always appends 'Confirm ... that it is {started|queued} and supervised — you will report back here' for a resolved-agent ASSIGN. But the supervision is decided LATER in the handler: US-005 supports a not-supervised outcome — when config.AUTO_TICKET_WATCH is off, create_board_task returns supervised=False and supervision='not supervised (AUTO_TICKET_WATCH is off)' (handlers_board_tasks.py:183-185) — and the watch can also legitimately fail to attach (dial off, or auto_create_ticket_watch returns None). The directive is built at api/chat.py dispatch time and never consults the dial, so it deterministically instructs Auto to CLAIM supervision even in the dial-off case, contradicting the tool result and the standing 'loud, honest visible activation' feedback (the whole point of the confirmation line). Fix direction: the directive must not hardcode a 'supervised' assertion; it must instruct Auto to state supervision status FROM the platform_create_task result's supervised/supervision fields, so the dial-off case confirms honestly (no false 'I will report back here').
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — build_assign_directive (auto.py) step 3 no longer appends 'and supervised — you'll report back here'. It now confirms the task id + started/queued, then instructs Auto to 'state its supervision status by echoing the platform_create_task result's 'supervision' field … Do NOT claim it is supervised unless that field says so.' The create result carries supervision='not supervised (AUTO_TICKET_WATCH is off)' when the dial is off (handlers_board_tasks.py:184-185) and 'supervised — I'll report back here …' when a watch attaches (:203-205), so the confirmation is honest in both cases. Docstring notes the RVW-3 rationale.

userStories.title: [MEDIUM] Agent-name resolution silently picks on ambiguity / ignores active-status at the write layer — bypasses the ask-in-thread contract
userStories.description: RE-REVIEW FINDING (chain 2/6 adversarial re-review + code-reviewer, both independent). The PRD's core guarantee — an ambiguous OR unknown agent name makes Auto ASK in-thread, never silently pick — is enforced only in AutoBrain and only partially. TWO gaps. (a) AutoBrain._match_roster_agent's EXACT-match loop (orchestrator/consumers/chatbot/auto.py:932-934: 'for a in agents: if name.lower()==target: return a.id, a.name') returns the FIRST exact hit with NO ambiguity check — unlike its own contains-fallback three lines below (:938-946), which the P224-RVW-1 fix made dedup-by-id and resolve only on exactly-one match. _active_agents() (:893-905) has no order_by, so with two ACTIVE agents sharing a case-insensitive name the pick is Postgres-row-order-dependent. Agent.name has NO unique DB constraint (core/models/core.py:212 uniques only (workspace_id,slug)); the app-layer guards that would block a duplicate (api/agents.py:368-371 create, modules/tools/discovery/cascade_installer.py:91-97 clone) compare Agent.name == name CASE-SENSITIVELY, while _match_roster_agent matches CASE-INSENSITIVELY — so 'Atlas' + 'atlas' both pass the guards yet collide here (also reachable via any non-API agent-creation path). (b) create_board_task (orchestrator/modules/tools/discovery/handlers_board_tasks.py:85-88) and assign_board_task (:341-344) re-resolve assigned_agent_name with sa_func.lower(Agent.name)==agent_name.lower()).first() — NO status filter and NO ambiguity check, a strictly weaker query than AutoBrain's active-only match. So even when AutoBrain cleanly resolved the ACTIVE 'Atlas' (id=7) and Auto told the user it assigned to it, the DB write can '.first()' a different same-named agent — e.g. an INACTIVE 'Atlas' (id=99) — instead: the roster the classifier reasoned over (active-only) and the roster the write assigns from (all statuses) diverge. Wrong outcome: a board ticket assigned to a different (or deactivated) agent than the one Auto resolved and confirmed, with no ask-in-thread — the wrong-agent-dispatch class the PRD exists to prevent. Fix direction: (a) give the exact-match loop the SAME dedup-by-id / exactly-one-or-ask guard the contains fallback has (0 or >=2 distinct exact matches -> (None, None)); (b) make create_board_task/assign_board_task resolve against ACTIVE agents and refuse or surface an ambiguity error on >1 match rather than silently .first(), so the write layer honors the same contract as the classifier.
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — _match_roster_agent (auto.py): the EXACT-name loop now collects every case-insensitive exact hit into a dict keyed by agent id and resolves ONLY when exactly one distinct agent matches; 0 or >=2 return (None, None), order-independent (never first-row) — the same guard the P224-RVW-1 contains fallback got three lines below. An exact hit still short-circuits the contains stage. Existing exact/contains tests stay green (test_match_roster_contains_possessive + RVW-1 ambiguity tests).

DONE — new module-level _resolve_active_agent_by_name(db, workspace_id, name) fetches the status=='active' roster (the same source AutoBrain._active_agents uses), matches the name case-insensitively in Python, dedups by agent id, and returns (agent, error): exactly-one -> (agent, None); none -> (None, None) [caller leaves the ticket unassigned / returns 'not found']; >=2 -> (None, 'Multiple active agents named …') so the caller REFUSES rather than .first()-ing a row-order pick. create_board_task and assign_board_task both call it; the old sa_func.lower(Agent.name)==name.lower().first() (no status filter, no ambiguity check) is deleted from both. Single-match and no-match behavior unchanged. (The list_board_tasks name FILTER keeps its .first() — a read filter, not a dispatch, and outside this finding's write-layer scope.)

DONE — tests/test_prd224_assign_lane.py +4 (exact loop): test_match_roster_exact_duplicate_asks_not_guesses ('Atlas'+'atlas' -> (None,None)), _exact_duplicate_is_order_independent (both roster orders -> None), _single_exact_still_resolves_amid_others ('atlas' -> (3,'Atlas') amid a Researcher), _exact_wins_over_contains_ambiguity. tests/test_board_task_handlers.py +7 (write layer): rvw4_create/assign_ambiguous_active_name_refuses (success False, 'Multiple active agents', zero commit/assign/NOTIFY), rvw4_create/assign_resolves_active_over_inactive_same_name (assigns the ACTIVE id=7, never the inactive id=99), rvw4_create_no_active_match_leaves_unassigned (inbox, no dispatch), rvw4_assign_no_active_match_is_not_found, rvw4_single_active_match_still_resolves.

userStories.title: [HIGH] ASSIGN immediate-start can STILL double-execute — the inline in_progress launch is not atomic against the board dispatcher's claim (RVW-2 residual)
userStories.description: RE-REVIEW FINDING (chain 2/6 adversarial re-review + code-reviewer, both independent). P224-RVW-2 added an old_status != 'in_progress' guard (orchestrator/modules/tools/discovery/handlers_board_tasks.py:430) meant to stop the ASSIGN 'start now' path from double-launching. It does NOT fully close the race: old_status is read from an UNLOCKED pre-commit SELECT (:393-400 — plain .filter().first(), no with_for_update) and BoardTask has NO version column, so update_board_task_status's own db.commit() (:414) is a blind PK-only UPDATE with no status precondition. Concrete interleaving: the imperative ASSIGN start fires two back-to-back tool calls — platform_create_task lands the ticket 'assigned' and US-001's _notify_dispatch_safe (:164-165) NOTIFYs board_dispatcher immediately, then platform_update_task_status -> 'in_progress'. If update_board_task_status's unlocked SELECT reads 'assigned' BEFORE board_dispatcher.claim_tasks (services/board_dispatcher.py:100/142 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, launch at :472-474) commits its claim, old_status is captured 'assigned', the :430 guard passes, and _launch_task_execution fires inline (launch #1) while the dispatcher also claims-and-launches (launch #2). _launch_task_execution._run() calls factory.execute_with_prompt UNCONDITIONALLY (orchestrator/api/board_tasks.py:1168); its status check (:1195-1196 'if task.status==in_progress') gates only the terminal DB write, NOT the side-effecting run. Wrong outcome: the assigned agent's REAL side effects (chase-invoice emails, external API calls, writes) execute TWICE — exactly the harm RVW-2 targeted. The window is not incidental: US-001's NOTIFY is designed to wake the dispatcher at the very moment Auto issues step-2, so the two launch mechanisms actively race (BOARD_DISPATCH_ENABLED defaults true; the loop starts in main.py). Fix direction: make the inline in_progress transition atomic — claim with a conditional UPDATE ... WHERE id=:id AND status='assigned' (or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE then re-check) and launch inline ONLY if THIS call won the assigned->in_progress transition, so exactly one of {inline, dispatcher} ever calls execute_with_prompt for a given claim. Mirror board_dispatcher.claim_tasks' own atomic-claim idiom rather than a stale unlocked read.
acceptanceCriteria: The inline in_progress launch in update_board_task_status fires only when THIS transaction atomically transitioned the row assigned->in_progress (conditional update / row lock + re-check), never on a stale pre-commit old_status read. A concurrent dispatcher claim + chat in_progress write yields EXACTLY ONE execute_with_prompt for the task.

test (concurrency-simulated at the handler level, no real Postgres needed): simulate the dispatcher having already claimed the row (status flipped to in_progress by another actor) between the SELECT and the write -> update_board_task_status launches ZERO inline executions and triggered_execution is False; the normal sole-launcher path (no competing claim) still launches exactly once.
watch_actions.run_board_task_action's existing in_progress guard (RVW-2) stays; no regression to the shared _redispatch_task path.
bash scripts/ralph/acceptance-prd224.sh -> EXIT=0; the RVW-2 tests (test_rvw2_*) stay green or are tightened to assert the atomic-claim behavior.

userStories.title: [MEDIUM] Watch-attach failure with AUTO_TICKET_WATCH ON leaves the create result with no supervision signal — no honest fallback
userStories.description: RE-REVIEW FINDING (chain 2/6 adversarial re-review + code-reviewer, both independent). In create_board_task's US-005 block (orchestrator/modules/tools/discovery/handlers_board_tasks.py:192-205), when the dial is ON but auto_create_ticket_watch returns None, NEITHER result['supervised'] NOR result['supervision'] is set — there is no else. auto_create_ticket_watch is deliberately fail-soft (orchestrator/modules/tools/discovery/handlers_watches.py:475-535: a bare except Exception -> return None around WatchService.create_watch), so any internal failure (transient DB error, a session already poisoned by an earlier failed flush in the same request, an unexpected raise) silently yields None. The P224-RVW-3 directive tells Auto to state supervision by echoing the result's 'supervision' field and to NOT claim supervision unless that field says so — so on this path Auto correctly makes no FALSE claim, but the ticket runs UNWATCHED with no report-back and the user is told nothing. Contrast the dial-OFF path (:183-185) which DOES set an honest 'not supervised (AUTO_TICKET_WATCH is off)'. US-005's own AC is 'when off, no watch and SAYS SO'; the attach-failure-while-ON case is the same 'must not silently skip supervision' requirement for a different precondition, and it is unhandled. Fix direction: add the else branch so a None watch under an ON dial sets result['supervised']=False + an honest result['supervision'] (e.g. 'supervision unavailable — the ticket will run unwatched'), so the confirmation is honest in the attach-failure case too.
acceptanceCriteria: create_board_task: when params['_assign_lane'] + assigned_agent_id and AUTO_TICKET_WATCH is ON but auto_create_ticket_watch returns None, result['supervised'] is False and result['supervision'] is a non-empty honest message that does NOT claim the ticket is supervised.
the watch-attached (supervised True) and dial-off (supervised False, 'AUTO_TICKET_WATCH is off') paths are unchanged.

test: monkeypatch auto_create_ticket_watch to return None with the dial ON -> create_board_task result has supervised False and a supervision message; assert the message does not falsely claim supervision.
